item.title: Trump Wants to Give Out $5,000 Checks. Is That Possible?
item.description: The president’s pledge to hand every American adult a “dividend” if Republicans keep control of Congress in the midterm elections raises questions.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:description: President Trump stands onstage during the Republican midterm convention in Dallas on Wednesday night.

item.title: D.O.J. Escalates Threats to States in Battle for Election Records
item.description: The department sent letters to at least 30 states demanding they retain election records, an outgrowth of President Trump’s baseless claims of widespread election fraud.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti
item.media:credit: Mark Abramson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Workers at the Los Angeles County election center in November 2024. The Department of Justice sued about 30 states to force them to send unredacted voter lists in its efforts to find widespread fraud.

item.title: Down in the Polls, Republicans Embrace a Familiar Tool: Fear
item.description: At an unusual midterm gathering, President Trump and his allies painted Democrats as dangerously un-American.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer
item.media:description: Representative Steve Scalise of Louisiana warned of a “Bolshevik Revolution in the Democratic Party.”

item.title: Trump Floats $5,000 ‘Trump Dividend’ Checks if Republicans Win the Midterms
item.description: In his convention speech, the president floated a $5,000 “Trump Dividend” for every adult American if Republicans keep control of Congress. The idea, like many others, may not come to pass.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers
item.media:description: President Trump has repeatedly dangled sizable payments to Americans that have not materialized.

item.title: ‘Pretend That I Am Running’: 7 Takeaways From the G.O.P. Midterm Convention
item.description: At a first-of-its-kind midterm convention, President Trump mostly offered retreads and self-congratulation. Then, he offered to pay Americans $5,000 apiece if Republicans kept power.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei and Shane Goldmacher
item.media:description: President Trump and his allies tried to gin up enthusiasm among MAGA voters who tend to go to the polls in presidential elections but not in midterms.

item.title: Trump’s Promise of $5,000 Dividend Checks Follows Past Cash Pledges That Never Materialized

item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:description: President Trump speaking during the first night of the Republican midterm convention, where he promised to give Americans a $5,000 “dividend” if Republicans retain control of Congress.

item.title: Trump’s Census Overhaul Would Exclude Some Immigrants and Remove Questions on Race
item.description: The proposals for 2030 are among significant changes that would upend a process for helping allot congressional seats and shape policies that address disparities.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs

item.media:description: A naturalization ceremony at Ellis Island in 2022. The Trump administration has proposed new census regulations that would no longer ask Americans about race, ethnicity and sexual orientation, and would exclude noncitizens without green cards.
